direction.comments: The direction on a macro scale is very silly, as the movie plays like a live-action cartoon with many '60s comedy and cartoon flavors; The direction on a micro scale is quite typical of the '60s; Storytelling is fairly linear and standard for a '60s comedy;

cast.comments: there isn't that much of a supporting cast, but its worth mentioning here how insane it was to get such an all-star cast in this movie as almost everyone in this movie was a major star of the 60s

story.comments: The concept is quite funny and unique, showing how the protagonist fails upward through her five marriages, as all she wants is a contented life despite constantly becoming wealthy; The plot structure is fairly linear and broken into chapters for each marriage, periodically returning to the end, which is similar to the structure of "The Other Guys"; Character writing is fun, as it shows how career-motivated her husbands become and how that leads to their demise, with the lead just wanting to be content in a quiet life like Thoreau;

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is quite typical of the '60s, being silly and comedic; The humor is fairly cartoonish and silly, feeling like a '60s cartoon come to life as if each joke were a Family Guy cutaway; The symbolism is quite simple, showing how the protagonist just wants a simple life away from the wealth and fame that ended her four marriages; The movie's symbolism boils down to Thoreau and wanting to live in a quiet home away from everything; The foreshadowing is very straightforward given how the plot is structured, though they do allude to the ending at the beginning;

score.comments: The score is very typical of the '60s;

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack is very typical of the '60s;

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is very typical of the '60s in its techniques and technology;

editing.comments: The editing is very typical of the '60s in its techniques and technology, as it uses many fades and old-school cuts; Splicing the different skits and cutaways, while aligning them with the changes in frame rates, helped make this movie feel very cartoonish;

sound.comments: The foley is very typical of the '60s; Visual effects are pretty good; The sound is very typical of the '60s;

visual_effects.comments: The visual effects are very typical of the '60s;

production_design.comments: This movie is very well designed from an artistic standpoint, as it acts as an example of how '60s cinema looked with its use of color and set design;

makeup.comments: The makeup helped complete the movie and the characters;

costumes.comments: Shirley MacLaine's costumes were very pretty and helped accentuate her as the true star of the show;

review.pacing: The pacing was very typical of the '60s;
review.climax: The climax was cute and wholesome;
review.tone: The tone is very typical of a '60s romantic comedy; The way this movie interjects skits and cutaways makes it feel like a '60s live-action cartoon and something one would see in Family Guy today;
review.overall: Overall, 'What a Way to Go!' is an entertaining romantic comedy that feels like a product of the 1960s, as it features a heavy-hitting all-star cast led by Shirley MacLaine and has handcrafted production design and costumes that feel lost in today's age; the comedy and tone of this movie make it entertaining, as it feels like a '60s cartoon brought to life with its silliness and cutaways
